chmmc-2010-fall-power-01a.prompt: Alice and Bob play a *pebbling game* on a finite connected graph $G$ (edges are undirected, there are no loops, and at most one edge joins two vertices). Alice takes $k$ pebbles, places them on the vertices in any way she wishes, and marks one vertex as the *target*. Bob wins if he can get at least one pebble onto the target using moves of this kind: choose a vertex $v$ with at least two pebbles, remove two pebbles from it, and place one of them on a neighbour of $v$ (the other is discarded). If the target already has a pebble at the start, Bob wins automatically. The *pebbling number* $\pi(G)$ is the least positive integer $k$ such that Bob can always win, no matter how Alice distributes the $k$ pebbles or chooses the target. Find the pebbling number $\pi(G_1)$ of the graph $G_1$ shown (a square with one diagonal, 4 vertices and 5 edges), and describe an initial configuration with one fewer pebble for which Bob does not win. (You do not need to prove your answer for this problem.)
